Save a figure as a static image

Source: R/kaleido.R
save_image.Rd

Exports a figure to PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG or PDF with the Python Kaleido package, using the plotly.js bundled with this package. Requires the reticulate package and a Python installation with kaleido (Kaleido 1.x also needs plotly and a Chrome browser): reticulate::py_install(c("kaleido", "plotly")).

Usage

save_image(p, file, ..., width = NULL, height = NULL, scale = NULL)

kaleido(...)

Arguments

p

A go_figure(), a figure from a px_*() function or a plotly htmlwidget (anything as_widget() accepts).

file

Output file; the format is taken from the extension (.png, .jpeg, .jpg, .webp, .svg or .pdf).

...

Unused.

width, height

Image size in pixels. Default: the figure's layout width and height, or 700 x 500.

scale

Multiplier for the image resolution (e.g. 2 for high-DPI PNGs).

Value

save_image() returns file invisibly. kaleido() returns a list with transform() and shutdown() functions.

Details

kaleido() returns an exporter whose transform(p, file, ...) function writes images; reuse it to export many figures without restarting Kaleido.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fig <- px_data_iris() |> px_scatter(x = ~sepal_width, y = ~sepal_length, color = ~species)
save_image(fig, tempfile(fileext = ".png"), width = 800, height = 500, scale = 2)
save_image(fig, tempfile(fileext = ".svg"))
} # }
